topic: European Landings in the New World
description: The first European expeditions to reach the Americas, and the earliest missions, forts, and towns that grew out of them — Spanish, Portuguese, English, French, and Dutch.

events.title: Columbus lands at San Salvador
events.desc: On his first voyage for Spain, Columbus made landfall on an island in the Bahamas he named San Salvador, believing he had reached the East Indies.

events.title: La Navidad founded
events.desc: After the Santa María ran aground off Hispaniola, Columbus left about 39 men behind in a small fort built from her timbers — the first Spanish settlement in the Americas. When he returned in November 1493, he found it burned and every man dead.

events.title: La Isabela founded
events.desc: On his second voyage, Columbus established a planned town on Hispaniola's north coast, the first organized European settlement in the New World, though it was abandoned within a few years.

events.title: Santo Domingo founded
events.desc: Columbus's brother Bartholomew founded Santo Domingo, which grew into the oldest continuously inhabited European-established city in the Americas.

events.title: John Cabot reaches Newfoundland
events.desc: Sailing for England's Henry VII, the Italian navigator Giovanni Caboto made landfall on the coast of Newfoundland, the first English claim in North America.

events.title: Columbus reaches South America
events.desc: On his third voyage, Columbus sighted the Paria Peninsula in present-day Venezuela, his first encounter with the American mainland.

events.title: Cabral claims Brazil for Portugal
events.desc: Pedro Álvares Cabral's fleet, blown off course en route to India, made landfall on the coast of Brazil and claimed it for the Portuguese crown.

events.title: Columbus reaches Central America
events.desc: On his fourth and final voyage, Columbus made landfall near present-day Trujillo, Honduras, his only contact with the Central American mainland.

events.title: Ponce de León lands in Florida
events.desc: Searching for new lands and, according to legend, a fountain of youth, the Spanish governor Juan Ponce de León landed on the coast of Florida and claimed it for Spain.

events.title: Balboa sights the Pacific Ocean
events.desc: Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama and became the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas, disproving the idea that the New World was part of Asia.

events.title: Cortés lands at Veracruz
events.desc: Hernán Cortés landed on the Gulf coast of Mexico and founded a fortified town before marching inland, beginning the conquest of the Aztec Empire.

events.title: Magellan's fleet winters in Patagonia
events.desc: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition made landfall at Puerto San Julián on the Patagonian coast to wait out the southern winter before pushing on toward the strait that now bears his name.

events.title: Verrazzano enters New York Harbor
events.desc: Sailing for France, Giovanni da Verrazzano became the first known European to enter the harbor later occupied by New Amsterdam and New York.

events.title: Cartier claims Canada for France
events.desc: Jacques Cartier planted a cross at the Gaspé Peninsula and claimed the surrounding land for the French crown, opening the way for later settlement along the St. Lawrence.

events.title: De Soto lands in Florida
events.desc: Hernando de Soto landed near Tampa Bay with a large expedition, beginning a four-year trek across the southeastern interior of North America.

events.title: Coronado reaches the Southwest
events.desc: Francisco Vázquez de Coronado's expedition reached the Zuni pueblos of present-day New Mexico while searching for the legendary golden cities of Cíbola.

events.title: De Soto reaches the Mississippi River
events.desc: De Soto's expedition became the first documented European party to reach the Mississippi River, near present-day Memphis.

events.title: St. Augustine founded
events.desc: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés founded St. Augustine for Spain, which remains the oldest continuously occupied European-founded city in the continental United States.

events.title: Roanoke Colony founded
events.desc: English colonists backed by Sir Walter Raleigh established a settlement on Roanoke Island, the first English attempt at a permanent colony in America.

events.title: Roanoke resettled; Virginia Dare born
events.desc: A second group of English colonists resettled Roanoke; among them, Virginia Dare became the first English child born in the Americas.

events.title: Roanoke found abandoned
events.desc: A relief expedition returned to find the colony deserted, with no sign of struggle and only the word "CROATOAN" carved into a post — the fate of the settlers remains unknown.

events.title: Jamestown founded
events.desc: English colonists established Jamestown in Virginia, which became the first permanent English settlement in North America.

events.title: Quebec City founded
events.desc: Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec as a fur-trading post for France, the foundation of New France in North America.

events.title: Santa Fe founded
events.desc: Spanish colonists founded Santa Fe as the capital of the province of Nuevo México, making it the oldest state capital in the present-day United States.

events.title: Plymouth Colony founded
events.desc: English Puritan separatists known as the Pilgrims, having crossed on the Mayflower, established Plymouth Colony in present-day Massachusetts.

events.title: New Amsterdam founded
events.desc: The Dutch West India Company established a fortified trading settlement on Manhattan Island, the seed of what would become New York City.
